heading: 14.5 Built-in operations
text:
### 14.5 Built-in operations [LUNI.14.5]

`real(z)` and `imag(z)` return the real/imaginary component in `z`'s unit;
`abs(z)` returns the magnitude in `z`'s unit, implemented as
`distance.hypotenuse(real(z), imag(z))`; `arg(z)` returns the phase angle as `radian`,
`atan2(imag(z), real(z))`; `conjugate(z)` returns `complex <unit>` (`a -
bi`); `exp(z)` returns `complex`, extended to accept a complex argument.

**Determinism class** per [LDET.3.3a]:

| Op | Class | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `real`, `imag`, `conjugate` | EXACT | field access / sign flip — basic ops |
| `+`, `-`, `*` (where annotated valid) | EXACT | basic IEEE 754, correctly-rounded |
| `abs(z)` | EXACT | computed as `distance.hypotenuse(real(z), imag(z))` ([LEXP.5.5]) — avoids the squaring overflow/underflow of a naive `√(a²+b²)` |
| `arg(z)` | EXACT | one correctly-rounded `atan2(imag(z), real(z))` ([LEXP.3.9.2]) |
| `exp(z)` | EXACT | Euler's formula, decomposed as below |

**`exp(z)` is this composition, and no other.** For $z = a + bi$, with
$\circ(\cdot)$ the correctly-rounded result of one operation:

$$\operatorname{Re} \exp(z) = \circ\big(\circ(e^{a}) \times \circ(\cos b)\big), \qquad \operatorname{Im} \exp(z) = \circ\big(\circ(e^{a}) \times \circ(\sin b)\big)$$

$e^{a}$ is evaluated once and used in both products. The result is not the
correctly-rounded complex exponential, and it is identical on every conforming
engine because every step is fixed ([LDET.3.4.4]). At the special values each
step follows [LEXP.3.9.3] and [LDET.3.6.2], so `exp(inf + 0i)` has an imaginary
part of `inf × 0`, which is NaN.
